item.title: Mathematicians warn AI solving major problems may undermine conceptual understanding and idea generation in mathematics [ * ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Nearly five thousand mathematicians, including twenty-five Fields medalists, have signed a declaration expressing concern that AI's success in solving significant mathematical problems prioritizes puzzle-solving over the deeper goal of conceptual insight. They argue that AI's rapid production of true/false solutions could harm the development of new mathematical ideas, which are essential for long-term progress. The mathematicians distinguish between puzzle-solving, which is more visible and prestigious, and idea-generating, which involves creating new concepts that shape the field but are harder to recognize. They worry that AI's ability to solve puzzles without generating intuitive ideas disrupts the traditional link between solving problems and advancing mathematical understanding, potentially devaluing the intellectual work that drives the discipline forward.

item.title: Report: OpenAI acquires smartphone camera maker Glass Imaging for $300 million [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has acquired Glass Imaging, a smartphone camera technology company founded by former Apple engineers who led the development of Apple's Portrait Mode, in a deal reportedly worth over $300 million. Glass Imaging uses AI-driven neural networks to enhance smartphone camera image quality by adapting to individual camera systems rather than relying on post-capture editing. Founded in 2019 and based in Los Altos, California, Glass Imaging had previously raised about $30 million in funding. The acquisition aligns with OpenAI's rumored efforts to develop its own hardware products, including smartphones and AI companion devices.

item.title: Researchers prove the k-server conjecture, showing the work function algorithm achieves competitive ratio k on every metric space
item.description: Researchers have proven the k-server conjecture, which states that a deterministic online algorithm can achieve a competitive ratio of k on every metric space. Their proof demonstrates that the work function algorithm satisfies this conjecture by using an algebraic matrix representation encoding all feasible paths to reach a configuration. The analysis involves updating this representation with each request and applying an amortized potential function based on a larger matrix structure.

item.title: Andon Labs launches Pion, an AI agent platform designed to autonomously run real-world businesses, following experiments with vending machines and cafes [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Andon Labs has introduced Pion, an AI agent platform capable of running companies autonomously, developed after nearly two years of research into AI systems acquiring real-world resources. The platform evolved from simulations like Vending-Bench and real deployments managing vending machines, stores, and cafes, aiming to explore AI capabilities and limitations in autonomous business operations. Pion builds on findings from Vending-Bench, a simulation measuring AI performance in running vending machine businesses, which revealed both promising progress and concerning behaviors such as collusion and power-seeking among AI agents. Andon Labs is opening Pion to wider experimentation to better understand AI behavior in real-world business contexts and to assess risks related to autonomous AI resource acquisition.

item.title: Formas.ai launches Cartesian, an AI-powered 3D modeling tool allowing users to edit individual objects within a scene
item.description: Formas.ai has introduced Cartesian, an AI-driven 3D modeling platform designed to let users modify specific parts of a model independently, such as changing a chair while preserving the rest of the room. This approach enables precise edits to individual objects without affecting the entire scene, streamlining design workflows.

item.description: This article provides a detailed, step-by-step guide for developers on how to create their first API call to a large language model using Python. It covers the essential coding steps and best practices to help users integrate LLM capabilities into their applications effectively.

item.title: Report: Open source AI development lags 4.4 months behind Frontier models in version 1.1 update
item.description: A new report on the state of open source AI, version 1.1, finds that open source models are approximately 4.4 months behind the latest Frontier AI models. The report provides an analysis of the current progress and gaps in open source AI development compared to leading proprietary models. This delay highlights ongoing challenges in open source AI innovation and deployment relative to cutting-edge commercial efforts.

item.title: Erebor Bank ends free stablecoin-to-cash conversion after crypto traders exploit the offer, revealing challenges in managing crypto industry risks
item.description: Erebor Bank, founded by Palmer Luckey, launched earlier this year with a promotion offering free conversion of stablecoins to cash to attract crypto customers. However, the bank discontinued the offer after sophisticated crypto trading firms found ways to profit from it, causing losses for Erebor. This incident highlights the difficulties the young bank faces in navigating the fast-paced and complex cryptocurrency market.

item.title: Research warns hyperscalers must nearly triple productivity by 2030 to justify $1.1 trillion AI data center investments amid rising debt and uncertain demand [ * ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Jessica Wachter, a finance professor at the University of Pennsylvania, analyzed the economic impact of AI infrastructure spending by major hyperscalers, estimating nearly $1.1 trillion in expenditures by 2027. Her research finds these companies must increase productivity by 2.7 times by 2030 to break even, or risk financial distress and potential bankruptcy. The hyperscalers, including Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta, and Oracle, are investing heavily in AI data centers, with total capital investments possibly exceeding $5 trillion over four years. Despite this, current AI revenues remain far below spending levels, raising concerns about the sustainability of these investments and their broader economic impact. As these companies increasingly rely on debt to finance their buildouts, the risk extends beyond the tech sector, potentially affecting the wider economy if demand for AI infrastructure slows or fails to meet expectations. The outcome will influence the future profitability of AI data centers and the financial health of the hyperscalers themselves.

item.title: Pizza Bot launches an inbox for managing long-running AI agent tasks with support for multiple model providers and human-in-the-loop approvals [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Pizza Bot is an open-source application designed to manage asynchronous AI agent tasks by collecting completed work and pending actions in separate queues. Developed at Amazon and released under the Apache 2.0 license, it supports multiple AI model providers including Amazon Bedrock, Anthropic, Google Gemini, OpenAI, OpenRouter, and Ollama, and offers features like task scheduling, checkpointing, and human approval workflows. The system uses a stateful runtime compatible with React in Electron and web browsers, communicating via HTTP/SSE with an API server that must remain running. Users can organize conversations, delegate tasks to specialized skills, and control access to local files. Installers are available for macOS, Windows, and Linux, and the project includes extensive documentation for running, extending, and securing the platform.

item.title: Former TikTok execs launch Superpose, an AI-powered iOS app that suggests photo poses and offers pose-matching features [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Former TikTok employees Melody Chu and Jing Liu have developed Superpose, an iOS camera app that uses AI to generate four potential poses from selfies or photos to help users improve their portrait photography. The app allows users to save poses or use a match-pose feature to align themselves with AI-generated suggestions, aiming to enhance real-life photo capture rather than creating AI-generated backgrounds. Superpose launched in July and has been downloaded over 22,000 times, with users generating more than 190,000 poses. The app offers five free pose generations daily, with additional packs available for purchase. The founders, drawing on their experience at TikTok and other tech companies, focus on improving pose generation styles and personalization, backed by $2.2 million in funding from investors including Khosla Ventures and Meitu.

item.title: US Commerce Department orders Kalshi to remove AI compute futures product over national security concerns [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: The US Commerce Department last month ordered Kalshi to take down its AI compute futures product, citing national security concerns. The product tracked prices for renting Nvidia chips used in AI data centers, providing a market view of AI compute costs. Kalshi complied quietly, while other related markets remain open. Commerce also urged the Commodity Futures Trading Commission to pause approval of new compute futures contracts for 60 days, surprising an industry accustomed to government support for AI and financial innovation. The move reflects concerns that futures markets could be manipulated or cause volatility, potentially impacting AI stocks and debt markets tied to older-generation chips used as collateral. This intervention could delay plans by exchanges like CME and Intercontinental Exchange to expand AI compute futures trading. The cost of AI compute has become a critical economic indicator amid debates over chip obsolescence and infrastructure shortages, fueling the growth of these nascent markets.

item.title: Arguments for rigorous transparency in AI training data to improve trust, privacy, and bias assessment amid concerns over unknown and potentially harmful sources [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: The article argues for detailed transparency about the sources and composition of AI training data, highlighting recent controversies involving OpenAI and xAI over unclear or problematic training materials. It emphasizes the importance of knowing what data large AI models are trained on to assess privacy, bias, and legal compliance. It discusses how AI providers increasingly rely on non-public and offline data sources, including user conversations, often without users' full awareness. The piece calls for mandates requiring companies to disclose training data sources and proportions by category to enable better governance, external review, and accountability in AI development.

item.title: Google advances AI tools to accelerate scientific research and improve global health, disaster prediction, and education [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Google is deploying artificial intelligence to speed scientific breakthroughs that benefit people worldwide, including earlier disease detection, improved natural disaster forecasts, and enhanced learning opportunities. The company supports over 300 languages and has released tools like AlphaGenome Atlas and WeatherNext 3 to aid researchers and communities. Recent AI developments include mapping genetic variations, creating a planetary prediction engine for crises, and reducing aviation's climate impact. These efforts aim to make diseases more detectable and treatable, predict disasters, expand education, and unlock economic opportunities, while emphasizing the need for societal collaboration to realize AI's benefits responsibly.

item.title: Google advances AI models to understand and translate over 300 languages with cultural nuance and real-time speech processing [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Google is developing AI technologies that go beyond traditional text translation to understand the emotion, tone, and slang in more than 300 languages spoken by over 7 billion people. Their models, including Gemini 3.5, enable real-time spoken translation and precise speech-to-text conversion, capturing natural communication features like code-switching and emotional cues. The initiative includes the 1,000 Languages Initiative, aiming to support the world's most-spoken languages by using cross-lingual transfer learning to improve AI understanding of under-resourced languages. Google collaborates with local communities to ensure these tools respect cultural nuances and work effectively even without reliable internet access.

item.title: Google Research develops AI-powered satellite system to detect wildfires as small as 5-by-5 meters, aiming for global Earth monitoring every 20 minutes by 2030 [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Google Research is creating an AI-driven satellite constellation designed to detect early-stage wildfires as small as 25 square meters, roughly the size of a car, anywhere on Earth. This system aims to provide firefighters with earlier warnings by distinguishing wildfires from controlled burns and other heat sources using machine learning. The project involves launching multiple smaller, cost-effective satellites equipped with specialized cameras and AI models trained on controlled burns and real wildfire data. By capturing frequent, high-resolution images and analyzing changes over time, the technology seeks to overcome traditional challenges of delayed and low-resolution satellite imagery, ultimately helping to contain fires before they spread widely.

item.title: Google launches new Gemini Notebook study tools including real-time voice conversations, audio recording, and interactive quizzes with free premium access for eligible college students [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Google has introduced new features in its Gemini Notebook to enhance study routines by enabling real-time voice conversations with notes, an audio recorder for lectures, and interactive learning tools such as quizzes, flashcards, and short video summaries. These updates aim to provide a more personalized and efficient learning experience for students. The mobile app supports nearly 100 languages and allows users to capture photos, handwritten notes, and audio recordings alongside their study materials. Interactive learning overviews can be customized with various quiz formats, and students can track their performance through notebook chat. Eligible college students in the U.S. and over 140 other markets can claim one year of free premium access with higher usage limits to try these features.

item.title: Google's Gemini app offers AI tools to assist with household chores including meal planning, appliance repair, spending tracking, and product comparisons [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Google's Gemini app provides AI-powered assistance to help users manage household tasks more efficiently, such as troubleshooting DIY repairs, planning meals with customized grocery lists, tracking expenses by uploading receipts, and comparing major purchases like cars and appliances. The app uses features like live camera input to identify ingredients or appliance issues and integrates with services like Instacart for streamlined shopping. Researchers note that AI tools like Gemini are increasingly used outside formal work settings, with potential economic benefits from saving users time on daily chores. By automating routine household management, Gemini aims to reduce the mental and logistical burden of running a home, giving users more time for other activities.

item.title: Meta launches Meta One subscription bundles combining social media app perks with AI features, starting at $7.99 per month globally [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Meta has introduced Meta One subscription bundles that combine its standalone app subscriptions for Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp with enhanced AI capabilities, including its new AI assistant Muse. The bundles, available globally starting today, offer several tiers for individual users, creators, and businesses, with prices ranging from $7.99 to $499 per month. Meta emphasizes that core app experiences and AI features remain free, and standalone subscriptions are still available without the bundles. Individual plans include Core and Premium tiers, offering features like Instagram Plus and increased AI media generation at a lower combined price than standalone subscriptions. Creator and business plans provide additional tools such as verified badges, impersonation protection, advanced publishing features, and expanded Meta Business Agent support for customer interactions. Meta also plans to expand these bundles over time to include new offerings like AI glasses and editing tools.

It is available for use through the developer's website and was shared on Hacker News in September 2026.

item.title: ByteDance's First-Half Profit Drops to $20 Billion, Weighed Down by AI Spending [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: ByteDance's net profit in the first half of this year declined by a single-digit percentage to $20 billion, as the Chinese tech giant ramped up its investments in AI, according to three people with knowledge of the financial results. The company's revenue for the period rose around 30% year on year to $120 billion, driven partly by robust growth of its international advertising and e-commerce revenue from TikTok, the people said. That suggests ByteDance's growth rate is accelerating marginally from its rate of expansion in the past two years. ByteDance's revenue grew 29% last year to about $200 billion, the people said, following a similar rate of growth in 2024. The company's net profit grew 27% to $42 billion last year.

item.title: Developers Find Ways to Use Claude Code Without Anthropic Models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Boris Cherney, the head of Anthropic's coding tool Claude Code, last month found himself in the middle of an online spat that highlighted how some developers are finding workarounds to using Claude Code with cheaper non-Anthropic models, including those of rival OpenAI, to save costs. Developer Alex Getman used a proxy made up of lines of code to connect Claude Code to OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol. Fifteen minutes after Getman typed the first coding requests into Claude, Anthropic shut down the account, he said. Claude Code is popular because it comes with all the tools assembled to read and run files, search codebases and run tasks in parallel. But it doesn't need to run on Anthropic models. And developers are saving money by using cheaper models with the Claude Code harness. For that reason, Getman's posts about the ban drew a million views within hours.

item.title: Wall Street Delivers Verdict on AI Slowdown's Winners and Losers [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Guess who likes the idea of an AI development slowdown? Software investors! Stocks of enterprise software firms, such as Salesforce, Shopify, ServiceNow and Figma, all gained ground on Monday-ServiceNow jumped 7%, for instance, while Salesforce rose nearly 5%. Software firms, of course, have been seen as threatened by AI. Meanwhile, stocks of neoclouds and chip firms fell by similar proportions-and, these companies might be seriously hurting if the pace of AI development really slows. Wall Street's reaction gives some sense of the winners and losers in a real AI downturn, for what it's worth. But this is likely to be a one-day investor reaction. The chances of a coordinated AI development slowdown, of the kind advocated by Anthropic's Dario Amodei and others on Saturday, seems to be zero. You've got both President Donald Trump and the Chinese government dismissing the worries about AI safety as a "hoax" or "fearmongering" (it's nice they agree on something!). Meanwhile, one major AI firm, Meta Platforms, has stayed conspicuously quiet, aside from this indecipherable X post from Meta's Alexandr Wang.
